# The containers macOS is asked to judge, one line each: its name, block size, bytes, release
# profile, the instant it records as seconds and nanoseconds since 1970, the root directory's
# owner and group, the program name in hex, its volumes in slot order as kind:name-in-hex, each
# followed by :name-in-hex of the volume's root snapshot where it has one and led by system/ or
# data/ where it is that member of a volume group, what each volume holds in slot order, the
# change made to it after it is written, the first 64 bits of the
# SHA-256 of its nonzero blocks with each preceded by its index as a little-endian u64, what
# macOS is expected to make of it, and the releases whose batch found that.
#
# What each volume holds is comma-separated, a volume past the list holding nothing, and the
# group's System volume's is followed by +firmlinks:N where it is given N firmlinks, /dK to dK
# for each K below N, of which those naming a directory at the root mark one. Each is `-`,
# nothing; tree:N:DIRS:SEED:MAX, the tree the populated
# gates generate from N entries under DIRS directories and SEED, no file larger than MAX bytes:
# directories, files, symbolic links, hard links, device nodes, pipes, sockets, attributes either
# side of 3,800 bytes, resource forks, names past ASCII, owners and times before 1970; or
# corpus:RELEASE:ROW:VOLUME:SHA256, a volume of the APFS corpus ci/fetch-apfs-corpus.sh pins,
# read back and changed as below. The rows named tree- hold a tree each: every block size but
# 8 KiB, a tree of three levels of small files, files past a mebibyte, objects far in, a
# populated volume beside two empty ones, and the shape of a root a RAM disk holds, one
# case-keeping volume named ramdisk.
#
# The rows named corpus- each hold a corpus volume, read from the container whose block dump has
# the SHA-256 SHA256, with what macOS wrote there on its own removed: the search index's
# directory, the event log's, and the attribute it sets on the root. Every regular file left is
# one the corpus probe's record of what it wrote names, with the content that record gives, and
# every attribute is one the probe sets. Then a file whose other names are hard links is removed,
# a compressed file and a directory are each replaced by a file held plain, three directories at
# the root are hidden, and the tree tree:60:4:109:70000 gives is added beneath /added. The other
# compressed files pass through as macOS wrote them. corpus-ramdisk has a root's shape too. Each
# keeps the probe's character device numbered 0,0, which fsck_apfs -W warns of on the containers
# macOS wrote as well, and which is the one warning these rows draw.
#
# The rows named fit- are each the size FormatPlan::fit gives the tree they hold, which a gate
# holds them to. fit-ramdisk has a root's shape and no room asked for, so its space manager
# records no block free, and macOS finds it full: every volume mounts read-write and refuses the
# probe's file for want of room. fit-v2 is two volumes at the smallest size with a slot for
# each. The other three are fitted with room for any user to write: fit-slack with
# Slack::Share(2000), a fifth of its blocks, fit-room-b4k with 64 MiB and fit-room-b64k with
# 256 MiB. Each is expected to take that room, room:BYTES: before the probe's file, the
# runner's own user writes that many bytes into the first volume, a mebibyte a write, and every
# write is taken.
#
# The rows named root- each give a volume a root snapshot: a root's shape, one named with 255
# bytes, the largest block size, and two volumes with one each, the second empty and its
# snapshot named past ASCII. Each snapshot is to be listed by its name, transaction and
# identifier, and to mount as the volume was written, before the probe writes its file to the
# volume and after.
#
# The rows named group- each join a System and a Data volume as a volume group: the System
# volume first with a root snapshot and firmlinks and both populated, the shape of a Mac's boot
# disk; the Data volume first, as diskutil makes a group, both populated; the largest block size
# on 27 with the System volume alone populated and firmlinked; and both empty, as diskutil makes
# one, Data first. Each container is to be listed as one group of its two volumes under the
# Data volume's identifier, both volumes mounted, the System volume's snapshot listed and mounted
# where it has one, and its firmlinked directories read back through its own mount.
#
# The container's identifier is the first 16 bytes of the SHA-256 of `container NAME`, and the
# identifier of the volume in slot K is that of `volume K NAME`, and of its root snapshot that
# of `snapshot K NAME`, each with the version and variant bits of a random identifier.
#
# The rows named bNk-pR-SIZE-vN-KIND are a covering array. Every pair of values of the block
# size, the profile, the size, the volume count and the first volume's name kind is in one of
# them, but for the two pairs no container of 1,024 blocks holds: two volumes and five. floor is
# 1,024 blocks, mid is 4 GiB, and far is past the contiguous limit, at a size where a free queue
# absorbs one of its keys. Volumes alternate kinds from the first. The edge rows take one input
# each to its limit. edge-late's time is later than any runner's clock, which fsck_apfs -W
# warns of.
#
# A change is made in the newest checkpoint: `-` is none, `checksum` one byte of the first
# volume's superblock, whose checksum is left as it was, and QUEUE-limit:N the node limit of
# the internal pool's free queue or the main device's, set to N in a space manager checksummed
# again. The limit rows hold one limit each against the one the writer gives: 116 for the main
# queue and 1 for the pool's at 1 GiB in 4 KiB blocks, where two mebibytes of nodes is 512,
# and 8 for the main queue at 16 GiB in 64 KiB blocks, where it is 32. macOS mounts each of
# them at the checkpoint before the one changed, which holds no volume.
